title: Porismata I: highest beatitude is not fleshly pleasure or fortune's secondaries
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): plus keeps a strange constancy in its very mutability. makes men insolent; afflicts together with great sadness; entangles ye most prudently planned together with ye worst outcomes; (2) Nor stands as it in secondary things subject to divine providence — because it blinds mortals; || (1) Man's highest beatitude stands as not ye pleasure belonging toward ye flesh. From this ye following porismata stand as inferred. II.
pass_b_english: II. From this the following porismata are inferred. (1) Man's highest beatitude is not the pleasure of the flesh.

(2) Nor is it in secondary things subject to divine providence — because it blinds mortals; entangles the most prudently planned with the worst outcomes; afflicts with great sadness; makes men insolent; and keeps a strange constancy in its very mutability.
source_text: II. Hinc inferuntur sequentia porismata. 1. Summa hominis beatitudo non est voluptas carnis. 2. Neque est in rebus secundis divinae providentiae subjectis — quia mortales caecos reddit; prudentissime cogitata pessimis successibus implicat; ingenti tristitia afficit; facit ut insololescant; variam in mutabilitate constantiam servat.
